scenario: WIBTA for lying to my brother for the rest of our lives about having a disorder? | My brother who is 2 years younger than me has Aspberger's. We have known for years but it's not something that we talk about in my family because my brother is embarrassed of it in a way. He is EXTREMELY smart and always has been. He excels in math and physics and everything in between. He is going to college and taking hard classes that he does well in. Lately, he has been depressed. More than depressed. A couple of months ago, he tried to take his own life by getting drunk and swallowing a bottle of acetaminophen. He and I are extremely close and he only talks to me. He called me in a panic hours after doing this and I took him to the hospital. He went to outpatient treatment after getting discharged from inpatient. The nurse had called me and asked if my brother was diagnosed with autism ever because he shows some clear signs. I talked to my brother about it today and he is still somewhat denying that he has autism. My brother loves me to death and I love him just as much. He has always looked up to me. I can't imagine a world without him. He loves how much more alike we get as we get older. He constantly says it with a big smile on his face. I have tried to talk to him about his autism and how he shouldn't be ashamed and he should own that about himself because some people don't even realize he has bad communication skills and he's so damn smart. Occasionally, his bad communication skills are very apparent and his disorder is obvious in other ways as well. I try to tell him that people say Mark Zuckerberg and Steve Jobs have Aspberger's but it doesn't do much for him when I say that. I feel if I tell my brother I have Aspberger's as well he would learn to love it and not deny it anymore, possibly helping himself. Would I be an asshole if I live a lie for the rest of my life to make my brother feel he's not alone and possibly help him move forward in life?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to lie to my brother about having a disorder, specifically Asperger's, for the rest of our lives. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My brother is two years younger than me and has Asperger's. We've known about this for years, but it's not something we talk about in our family because he's embarrassed about it. Despite having Asperger's, he's extremely smart, excels in math and physics, and is doing well in college. However, he's been really depressed lately, and a couple of months ago, he tried to take his own life by getting drunk and swallowing a bottle of acetaminophen. He called me in a panic, and I took him to the hospital. After that, he went through outpatient treatment. Recently, a nurse asked me if my brother was diagnosed with autism because she noticed some clear signs. I talked to my brother about it today, and he's still denying that he has autism. He loves me a lot, and I love him just as much. We've always been close, and as we get older, we're becoming more alike, which he really likes. I've tried talking to him about his autism and how he shouldn't be ashamed of it. I've mentioned that some people think Mark Zuckerberg and Steve Jobs have Asperger's, but that doesn't seem to help him. I'm considering telling him that I have Asperger's too, thinking that it might help him accept his own diagnosis and not feel alone. But I'm wondering if lying about this would make me a bad person. First, I need to understand why my brother is denying his diagnosis. Maybe he feels ashamed or doesn't want to be labeled. I can see why someone would feel that way, especially if society has negative perceptions about autism or Asperger's. But I also know that being honest is important in relationships. If I lie to him about having Asperger's, what are the potential consequences? On one hand, it might make him feel less alone and more accepted. On the other hand, lying could damage our trust and make things worse if he finds out the truth later. I also need to consider whether there are other ways to help him without lying. Maybe I can find resources or support groups where he can connect with others who have Asperger's. Or perhaps I can encourage him to seek counseling or talk to someone who specializes in autism. Another thing to think about is the impact of my actions on myself. If I lie to him, would I feel guilty or dishonest? It's important to maintain my own integrity and ensure that I'm making decisions that align with my values. I should also think about the long-term effects of this lie. If I tell him I have Asperger's, and he believes me, how would that affect our relationship in the future? Would it help him in the long run, or could it cause more confusion or issues? Maybe I can approach this by being honest but compassionate. I can express my concern for him and let him know that I'm here to support him, whether he chooses to accept his diagnosis or not. I can also share information about successful people who have Asperger's to help him see that it's not something to be ashamed of. I should also consider talking to a professional, like a counselor or therapist, who can provide guidance on how to approach this sensitive topic with my brother. They might have strategies or advice that I haven't thought of. In summary, while my intention is to help my brother feel less alone and more accepted, lying about having Asperger's might not be the best approach. It could lead to trust issues and might not address the underlying reasons for his denial. Instead, focusing on honest communication, providing support, and seeking professional advice might be more effective in helping him move forward.
